citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the autocorrelation, PACF, AR and Ljung-Box cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioAnalysis::adfTest(lag=1): regress the first difference on a constant, the lagged level and 1 lagged difference; the ADF statistic is the t-statistic on the lagged-level coefficient. The reference re-computes it with statsmodels.tsa.stattools.adfuller(autolag=None, regression=c) on the identical signal, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the autocorrelation, PACF, AR and Ljung-Box cases). The Augmented Dickey-Fuller test checks for a unit root (random-walk drift / non-stationarity): a large negative statistic rejects the unit-root null in favour of stationarity. adfTest is a NEW op adding the stationarity test the ecosystem lacked (and which the ACF/PACF/AR folds implicitly assumed). Its STATISTIC reproduces statsmodels.tsa.stattools.adfuller(autolag=None) BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~7e-15) -- an exact OLS regression quantity. HONEST caveat: only the statistic is bit-exact; the ADF critical values and p-value require the Dickey-Fuller / MacKinnon response-surface reference tables (an approximation), so this op does NOT compute them -- the decision here compares the statistic against statsmodels tabulated 5% critical value. Finding: the statistic (-22.36) is ~19.5 below the 5% critical value (-2.86), decisively rejecting the unit-root null: the eyes-closed EEG segment is stationary (no drift over 10 s), retroactively justifying the stationarity assumption of the companion ACF/PACF/AR/Ljung-Box folds.
